publisher: OpenCorporates Ltd (aggregator of official state SOS company registers)
native_identifiability: NOT a Native-business source — a VALIDATION layer: ~100M US companies + ~190M officers unified from all 50 states' official registers, with entity name, incorporation date, registered address and (where states disclose) director names, traceable to the source register
identity_semantics: Validation only: confirms a claimed business is a real registered entity, its standing, address and officers — it can corroborate or contradict a name/address on a TERO or chamber row. It CANNOT establish Native ownership: beneficial ownership is generally not in public US state records, and many states (e.g. Delaware) do not disclose officers at all. Existence/officer match is evidence of the entity, never of tribal citizenship or ownership share
export: bulk downloads + API for a handful of states; most state systems are manual-lookup only (OpenCorporates is the aggregation layer over them)
notes: NEW FRAME: validation infrastructure (SOS registries / license boards). Use as the entity-resolution spine's corroboration layer — match a candidate Native business to its state registration to confirm it exists and pin its canonical name/address. do_not_infer: registration ≠ Native ownership. Fits Cedar's stated entity-layer method (identifier-first matching). nation_ids: [] (national validation tool).

source: FinCEN Beneficial Ownership Information (BOI) registry — CTA
publisher: U.S. Treasury, Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN)
native_identifiability: Would have been the one federal registry of who actually OWNS a company (beneficial owners ≥25% / substantial control) — the exact field missing from state SOS records
identity_semantics: HONEST NEGATIVE / PATH CLOSED for US Native businesses: the 2025-03-26 interim final rule (FR 2025-05199) exempts ALL entities created in the United States and their beneficial owners from reporting BOI. 'Reporting company' now means only FOREIGN-formed entities registered to do business in a US State or Tribal jurisdiction. So domestic tribally-owned and individually-Native-owned US entities do NOT file, and the registry is not a US-ownership-validation path. Access to filed BOI was never public anyway (law-enforcement/FI use)
export: none for this purpose — non-public registry, and US entities now exempt
notes: Recorded so the beneficial-ownership registry is not chased as an ownership-validation source: it is exempted for US entities and non-public regardless. NOTABLE SIDE LEAD: the CTA 'reporting company' definition explicitly names filing with 'a secretary of state or similar office' of a TRIBAL jurisdiction — confirming some tribes run their own business registries that function like a state SOS; those tribal registries are a separate ENUMERATION lead worth a future frame. nation_ids: [].
